req.title: Redirect count boundary
req.statement: The system shall accept /redirect/<n> with n in the range 1..30 inclusive and reject values above.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states /redirect/<n> accepts n in [1..30] inclusive and rejects values above 30. Key boundaries are: n=1 (lower bound), n=30 (upper bound), n=31 (first rejected value above upper bound). We also need a mid-range positive case (EP), a zero/negative case (NEG for assert n>0), and exact status code assertions. The source code shows: assert n > 0 (so n=0 triggers AssertionError/500), and the route uses int converter so non-integer paths return 404. For n>30, httpbin returns 404 based on its route guard. We test BVA at 1, 30, 31; EP at a mid-range value like 5; NEG at 0 and 31. The redirect chain means the first response is a 302 (redirect), and following all redirects eventually yields 200. We use follow_redirects=True to get the final 200 for positive cases, and check the raw 302 status for the first hop. For n=31 and above, httpbin returns 404. We assert exact status codes throughout.

tests.name: test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_positive
preconditions: n=1 is the minimum valid redirect count
expected: Response contains 'url' key in JSON body
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: n=1 is lower boundary of valid range [1..30]
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_positive():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'url' in data

test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_positive()
